title: Coral and the Hollow
premise: Rosalind Okonkwo carves messages from the dead into bone, but she has never left Hollowmere, a valley where magic cannot follow. When her first date in years, a cartographer named Theo Vance, appears by name in a century-old book of prophecies, he is wrenched through the valley's boundary into the world beyond — into the path of a king whose body has been hollowed and worn by an ancient parasite. Rosalind, the only person whose bone-carving can unbind a soul, must leave the valley for the first time, guided by Theo's letters carried back by the dead. In the end she unmakes the parasite by carving its true name into the king's own bone, but the act erases her memories of Theo — and he must choose to win her again from nothing.
about_author: O. M. Crane is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent years restoring carved ivory and bone, work that seeded a lifelong fascination with what objects remember. They live near the sea and write fantasy about the quiet violence of forgetting.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets Magic
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She carves a dying woman's last words into bone, establishing her gift and her isolation in Hollowmere, where magic cannot cross the boundary stones. A blind date looms — her first in years. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like a familiar coat.

chapters.title: A Date with Theo Vance
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The date with cartographer Theo Vance goes awkwardly well; he sketches maps of places he's never been, including a palace Rosalind recognizes from a carved bone. Emotional beat: cautious hope, the terror of being known.

chapters.title: The Book That Waited a Century
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In Hollowmere's archive, Theo finds a prophecy book dated 1897 that names him, tonight's date, and the phrase 'the hollow crown.' Before he can speak, the boundary pulls him through. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Gone Through the Stones
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Theo vanishes from the tavern mid-sentence; the dead whisper that he crossed where no living thing should. She finds his sketchbook, its last page showing the palace and her own name. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve igniting.

chapters.title: What the Dead Carry
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She learns the dead can carry messages across the boundary but not people. She carves her first letter to Theo into a rib bone and sends it with a recently dead courier. Emotional beat: grief repurposed as a tool.

chapters.title: The Kingdom of Ash and Salt
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo wakes in the kingdom beyond, where the parasite-king's soldiers harvest memory from villagers. He's mistaken for the prophecy's 'mapmaker' and taken to court. Emotional beat: displacement, the wrongness of being expected.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At court, Theo meets King Aldric — a man with a stranger's smile and eyes like empty rooms. The parasite wearing him speaks to Theo privately, offering passage home in exchange for the prophecy book's location. Emotional beat: horror masked by courtesy.

chapters.title: First Letter, Carved in Bone
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The dead courier reaches Theo with Rosalind's carved message: hold on, I'm coming. He learns the dead in this kingdom are enslaved by the parasite, their voices its surveillance network. Emotional beat: relief braided with fear.

chapters.title: The Bone-Carver's Exile
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Crossing the boundary, Rosalind's suppressed magic floods back painfully — in Hollowmere her hearing the dead was muffled; outside it's deafening. She's found by Sefa, a deserter soldier who recognizes bone-carvers as heretics. Emotional beat: overwhelm and unexpected alliance.

chapters.title: Maps of a Country That Lies
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Sefa's alternating POV. Sefa reveals the kingdom's maps are magically falsified; Theo's cartographer's instincts are the key to navigating the palace. Rosalind sends a second letter via the dead. Emotional beat: trust slowly built between strangers.

chapters.title: The Archive of Unmade Names
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo sneaks into the palace archive and discovers the parasite's method: it erases a king's name from every record, making the man replaceable. He finds Aldric's true name half-erased and copies it. Emotional beat: a scholar's weapon found.

chapters.title: Letters Across the Dark
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Theo's alternating POV, told through their carved and written messages. They coordinate: she will reach the palace during the Feast of Hollow Lights; he will get Aldric to her. Emotional beat: intimacy built entirely from borrowed voices.

chapters.title: The Feast of Hollow Lights
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the feast, the parasite publicly hollows a courtier who spoke out of turn, demonstrating its power. Theo realizes it suspects him and that time is shorter than planned. Emotional beat: terror in a room full of applause.

chapters.title: Sefa's Price
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa confesses she deserted after being ordered to harvest her own brother's memories. She agrees to open a servant's door into the palace, knowing it's a death sentence if caught. Emotional beat: atonement chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The King in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind reaches the palace and finds Aldric's original body — the parasite keeps the hollowed man alive in the cellars, a vessel it can re-wear. Aldric, barely lucid, begs her not to save him. Emotional beat: compassion versus a man's wish to end.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Boundary of Skin
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo is caught; the parasite offers him his memories of Rosalind in exchange for betraying her location. He refuses, and it begins eating his memories anyway. Emotional beat: identity under siege, love as the last unyielding thing.

chapters.title: What the Parasite Wants
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Through the enslaved dead, Rosalind learns the parasite's true name and origin: it was once a bone-carver who carved her own soul into a king to escape death. The parallel to Rosalind's gift is unmistakable. Emotional beat: horror at kinship with the monster.

chapters.title: The Rescue That Costs a Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind, Sefa, and Theo's alternating POV. Sefa's door opens; Rosalind frees Aldric's body while Theo, half-hollowed, barely recognizes her. They flee through falsified maps only his cartographer instincts can read. Emotional beat: desperate flight, love persisting through damage.

chapters.title: Carving the True Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, climax. Cornered at the palace's bone altar, Rosalind carves the parasite's true name into Aldric's living bone, unbinding king and parasite. The carving demands a price: her memories of Theo, the dearest thing she has. She carves anyway. Emotional beat: sacrifice at the height of the storm.

chapters.title: The King Remembers Himself
chapters.summary: Theo and Aldric's POV. The parasite unravels; Aldric returns, hollow-eyed but his own, and the enslaved dead are released. Theo, his memories shredded, looks at Rosalind and feels a grief for someone he cannot name. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Second Map
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo chooses to stay in the kingdom and help Aldric rebuild, drawing the first true maps. He begins keeping a journal of fragments about a woman with carving tools and a laugh he can almost hear. Emotional beat: rebuilding from absence.

chapters.title: Coral and the Hollow
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Months later, Rosalind returns to the valley, carrying Theo's journal. She carves their story into coral bone and reads it to him; the dead whisper that some names, once carved, can be carved again. He asks her out to dinner, as if for the first time. Emotional beat: found family and love chosen anew.
